## Research program

::: {.section-intro}
How can we obtain reliable inference when data structure is partly hidden, constrained by geometry or sensitive to numerical approximation? I develop model diagnostics and uncertainty quantification methods to address this question. My program connects probabilistic modelling, simulation, visualization and reproducible R software.
:::

::: {.link-list}
[Publications and preprints](#publications){.btn .btn-outline-dark}

:::

## Contributions and research themes

::: {.feature-grid}
::: {.research-card}
### Sequential models and latent states

My work with Thierry Duchesne, Louis-Paul Rivest and Daniel Fortin developed multi-state models for animal movement, published in [CSDA in 2017](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.csda.2016.07.009) and [AOAS in 2017](https://doi.org/10.1214/17-AOAS1045).

In [Beyond the next step (2026)](https://doi.org/10.1111/2041-210X.70313), I propose generative validation for step-selection functions: comparing simulated trajectories with the movement features that motivate the analysis. My preprints study sequential predictive diagnostics and uncertainty in latent-state sequences.

::: {.link-list}
[Viterbi tubes, preprint](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.17181){.btn .btn-outline-dark}
:::
:::

::: {.research-card}
### Directional statistics

With Louis-Paul Rivest, Thierry Duchesne and Daniel Fortin, I contributed to a [general angular regression model (2016)](https://doi.org/10.1111/rssc.12124). A [2026 preprint](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.06790) proposes an extension with a circular random intercept and a scalar random slope.

I also develop regression and visualization software connecting the geometry of circular, axial and toroidal data to the statistical questions being studied.

::: {.link-list}
[CircularRegression](packages/circularregression.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-dark}
[ggcircular](packages/ggcircular.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-dark}
:::
:::

::: {.research-card}
### Density and outlier diagnostics

With Thierry Duchesne and Michel Carbon, I develop a [leave-one-out influence diagnostic](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14335) for outlier detection based on linear-blend frequency polygons.

The GLBFP package provides the density estimation software base. Leave-one-out diagnostics are available in its GitHub development version. The presentation of this work received the [2026 SSC New Investigator Presentation Award](https://ssc.ca/en/awards/2026/aurelien-nicosia-new-investigator-presentation-award-2026).

::: {.link-list}
[GLBFP and release status](packages/glbfp.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-dark}
:::
:::
:::

## Future directions

The next stages of my program address three questions:

- Localizing failures in sequential models, representing multiple plausible latent trajectories and quantifying error introduced by Monte Carlo approximation.
- Developing diagnostics for hierarchical circular models and dependence tests adapted to circular and toroidal spaces.
- Studying the stability of density diagnostics across dimensions, tuning choices and sampling regimes, with reproducible comparisons of computational cost.

Animal movement is an established application area. Environmental sequences and sensor data are prospective extensions to be developed with domain specialists.

## Research training

I favour projects that begin with a focused question, a literature review and reproduction of existing results. Contributions can address theory, simulation, visualization or software validation. Each project should distinguish mathematical results, numerical evidence and open questions.

My experience includes undergraduate project advising, industry internship supervision and examination of master’s theses. Proposed graduate projects build on the three themes above. [Teaching and supervision](enseignement.qmd#supervision).

## Doctoral thesis

::: {.meta-list}
Title: General Multi-state Models for the Analysis of Animal Movement

Year: 2024

University: Université Laval

Supervisors: Thierry Duchesne and Louis-Paul Rivest
:::

This thesis develops a general framework for multi-state modeling of animal movement. It combines the rigor of hidden Markov models with the flexibility of habitat-selection functions, through a unifying formulation connecting behavioral and spatial approaches.

::: {.link-list}
[View thesis](https://corpus.ulaval.ca/server/api/core/bitstreams/cf3426a4-3475-4d48-a4c4-de29df846ed5/content){.btn .btn-outline-dark}
[Code and reproducible material](https://github.com/AurelienNicosiaULaval/multi-state-model-animal-movement){.btn .btn-outline-dark}
:::
